change.after: Parse all source blocks, then parse and compare only rebuilt result blocks
preserved: constructor rejection of non-text untouched blocks

verification.domScope: List router/controllers, toolbar/queue/adapter, synthetic clipboard/composition, exact undo/redo and V6 recovery, native IndexedDB/SHA-256 autosave and high-level startup/rollback/backup; not physical OS input
verification.packedConsumers: All three browser engines, base Node import, strict TypeScript and Chromium smoke passed against the same private installed artifacts

productionTiming.method: Sequential old/new/old/new qualified private installed-package runs; identical production-minified fixture/browser JS, fresh browser processes, no profiling or compilation overlap; three independent owners per size per engine
productionTiming.conclusion: Firefox 500-item edit medians were about 9% lower in both candidate runs against repeated 349 ms controls. Other engine differences were small/variable. Local evidence only, not multi-device or p95 qualification; latency remains open.
